title: Level 3 (Advanced) - A-17
notes:
West leads the ♠Q against 3NT. South has 7 top tricks (2 spades, the ♥A, and 4 diamonds). South can enventually develop a trick in clubs and at least 1 more trick in hearts. The defense has attacked spades, however, and South does not have time to get 2 more tricks in this way.

South must try to get 2 extra tricks in hearts. The heart combination contains a standard double finessing position. South should aim to succeed whenever East has either the ♥K or ♥Q (or both). South will use North's diamonds as entries to take the heart finesses. South should win the spade opening lead and test the diamond position by cashing 2 top honours in the closed hand.

When diamonds prove to be 3-2, South will be able to reach the North hand twice in diamonds. The remaining diamond honour is played from the closed hand and overtaken by the ♦A in the dummy.

It is important not to play the ♥J on the first round of the suit. A low heart is played from the dummy, South finessing. West will win (it is actually best defense for West to duck, forcing South to guess the heart position. Luckily almost nobody could find this play). After winning his heart honour, West will clear the spades.

South can now lead the ♦2 to dummy to play hearts again. The ♥J is now played from North. East must duck and South finesses. Due to South's foresight in not playing the ♥J on the first round of the suit, the lead remains in dummy to play hearts again through East.
